152|
153|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
154|
155|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
156|
157|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
158|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
159|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
160|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
161|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
162|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
163|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
164|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
165|
166|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
167|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
168|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
169|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
170|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
171|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
172|
173|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.
174|
175|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
176|
177|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
178|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
179|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
180|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
181|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.
182|
183|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
184|
185|### 6.1 The loop
186|
187|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
188|
189|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
190|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
191|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
192|- **Ending.**
193|
194|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
195|| --- | --- | --- |
196|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
197|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
198|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
199|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
200|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
201|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
202|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
203|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
204|
205|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
206|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
207|
208|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
209|
210|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
211|
212|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
213|| --- | --- | --- |
214|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
215|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
216|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
217|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
218|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
219|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
220|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
221|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
222|
223|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
224|
225|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
226|
227|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
228|| --- | --- | --- |
229|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
230|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
231|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
232|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |
233|
234|### 6.4 Action allowlist
235|
236|| Action | Notes |
237|| --- | --- |
238|| `connectorInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `intervalSeconds`, `parameters` |
239|| `connectorInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
240|| `connectorInstances.runOnDemand` | |
241|| `jobInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `parameters` |
242|| `jobInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
243|| `jobInstances.runOnDemand` | |
244|| `none` | No write: the fault has cleared (for example, after a human acted on an escalation). Goes straight to verification |
245|| `escalate` | Required when the fix is outside the allowlist (e.g. a credential rotation). Pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT |
246|
247|`connectorInstances.setLogsCollection` is not an action: turning on logging fixes nothing, so verification would fail it. The SRE can ask for it in an `escalationSummary`.
248|
249|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
250|
251|```json
252|{
253|  "incidentId": "string",
254|  "deployment": "string",
255|  "component": "string",
256|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
257|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
258|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
259|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
260|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
261|  "action": {
262|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
263|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
264|    "resource": "full resource name",
265|    "updateMask": ["field"],
266|    "patch": {},
267|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
268|  },
269|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
270|  "rollback": "string",
271|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
272|}
273|```
274|
275|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
276|
277|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
278|
279|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
280|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
281|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
282|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
283|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, the patch keys are within `updateMask`, and `resource` is the deployment's own connector instance (`connectorInstances.*`) or job instance (`jobInstances.*`). `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
284|
285|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
286|
287|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
288|
289|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
290|| --- | --- |
291|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
292|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
293|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
294|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
295|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
296|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
297|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |
298|
299|### 6.6 Guardrails
300|
301|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
302|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
303|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
304|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
305|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
306|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
307|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
308|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

334|

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check that every deliverable ID has a matching acceptance test."""

import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ID_RE = re.compile(r"\bD(\d+)-T(\d+)\b")
DIR_RE = re.compile(r"^d(\d+)$", re.IGNORECASE)
TEST_RE = re.compile(r"def\s+test_d(\d+)_t(\d+)_", re.IGNORECASE)


def collect_doc_ids(doc: Path) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
    text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    return {(int(n), int(m)) for n, m in ID_RE.findall(text)}


def existing_deliverables(tests_root: Path) -> set[int]:
    found: set[int] = set()
    if not tests_root.is_dir():
        return found
    for child in tests_root.iterdir():
        if child.is_dir():
            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
            if match:
                found.add(int(match.group(1)))
    return found


def collect_test_ids(tests_root: Path, deliverable: int) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
    found: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    target = None
    for child in tests_root.iterdir():
        if child.is_dir() and DIR_RE.match(child.name):
            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
            if match and int(match.group(1)) == deliverable:
                target = child
                break
    if target is None:
        return found
    for pyfile in target.rglob("*.py"):
        try:
            text = pyfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            continue
        for n, m in TEST_RE.findall(text):
            found.add((int(n), int(m)))
    return found


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Trace deliverable IDs to tests.")
    parser.add_argument("--doc", required=True, help="Path to deliverables doc")
    parser.add_argument("--tests", required=True, help="Root of acceptance tests")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    doc = Path(args.doc)
    tests_root = Path(args.tests)
    if not doc.is_file():
        print(f"doc not found: {doc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not tests_root.is_dir():
        print(f"tests root not found: {tests_root}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    doc_ids = collect_doc_ids(doc)
    present = existing_deliverables(tests_root)
    missing: list[str] = []
    for n, m in sorted(doc_ids):
        if n not in present:
            continue
        if (n, m) not in collect_test_ids(tests_root, n):
            missing.append(f"D{n}-T{m}")
    if missing:
        print("Missing tests for IDs:")
        for item in missing:
            print(f"  {item}")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

        if child.is_dir() and DIR_RE.match(child.name):
            match = DIR_RE.match(child.name)
            if match and int(match.group(1)) == deliverable:
                target = child
                break
    if target is None:
        return found
    for pyfile in target.rglob("*.py"):
        try:
            text = pyfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except OSError:
            continue
        for n, m in TEST_RE.findall(text):
            found.add((int(n), int(m)))
    return found


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Trace deliverable IDs to tests.")
    parser.add_argument("--doc", required=True, help="Path to deliverables doc")
    parser.add_argument("--tests", required=True, help="Root of acceptance tests")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    doc = Path(args.doc)
    tests_root = Path(args.tests)
    if not doc.is_file():
        print(f"doc not found: {doc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    if not tests_root.is_dir():
        print(f"tests root not found: {tests_root}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    doc_ids = collect_doc_ids(doc)
    present = existing_deliverables(tests_root)
    missing: list[str] = []
    for n, m in sorted(doc_ids):
        if n not in present:
            continue
        if (n, m) not in collect_test_ids(tests_root, n):
            missing.append(f"D{n}-T{m}")
    if missing:
        print("Missing tests for IDs:")
        for item in missing:
            print(f"  {item}")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

{"content":""""D7 acceptance tests: Cloud Logging adapters and the IAM air gap.

Covers deliverables.md §D7 rows T1, T7, T8 and T10, exactly as specified
in docs/d7-pins.md (Rows, pins 5-8). Every test is marked gcp and skips
when FLEETSRE_GCP_PROJECT is unset. Google packages are imported inside
the test functions, after the first D7 stub call, so with stubs in place
each test fails with NotImplementedError and needs neither infra nor
credentials (d7-pins 5).
"""

import ast
import json
import os
import time
import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SAMPLE_FILES = ("connector.jsonl", "etl.jsonl")
SUBSCRIPTION_ID = "fleet-sre-logs-obs"
READ_DEADLINE_S = 90
PULL_DEADLINE_S = 120
REFRESH_DEADLINE_S = 120
POLL_SLEEP_S = 2
T7_REWRITE_S = 15


def _tagged_samples(now: datetime) -> tuple[str, list[Any]]:
    """All connector+etl samples retagged with a fresh runId (d7-pins 5)."""
    from fleetsre.logmodel import read_jsonl

    run_id = f"d7-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    entries: list[Any] = []
    seq = 0
    for name in SAMPLE_FILES:
        path = ROOT / "fixtures" / "logs" / "samples" / name
        if not path.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing sample fixture: {path}")
        for entry in read_jsonl(path):
            seq += 1
            entry.timestamp = now
            entry.insertId = f"{run_id}-{seq}"
            entry.jsonPayload["runId"] = run_id
            entries.append(entry)
    return run_id, entries


def _refresh(creds: Any) -> None:
    """Refresh impersonated creds, retrying RefreshError to 120 s (d7-pins 5)."""
    import google.auth.exceptions
    import google.auth.transport.requests

    request = google.auth.transport.requests.Request()
    start = time.monotonic()
    while True:
        try:
            creds.refresh(request)
            return
        except google.auth.exceptions.RefreshError:
            if time.monotonic() - start >= REFRESH_DEADLINE_S:
                raise
            time.sleep(POLL_SLEEP_S)


def _retry_denied(call: Callable[[], Any], deadline_s: int) -> Any:
    """Run a positive call, retrying PermissionDenied to deadline (d7-pins 6)."""
    import google.api_core.exceptions

    start = time.monotonic()
    while True:
        try:
            return call()
        except google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied:
            if time.monotonic() - start >= deadline_s:
                raise
            time.sleep(POLL_SLEEP_S)


def _poll_entries(
    query: Any, start: datetime, end: datetime, want: set[str]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Poll query.entries until every wanted insertId is back (d7-pins 5-6)."""
    import google.api_core.exceptions

    deadline = time.monotonic() + READ_DEADLINE_S
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}
    while True:
        try:
            found = query.entries(start, end)
        except google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise
            time.sleep(POLL_SLEEP_S)
            continue
        seen = {entry.insertId: entry for entry in found}
        if all(insert_id in seen for insert_id in want):
            return seen
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            missing = sorted(set(want) - set(seen))
            raise AssertionError(f"timed out waiting for log read-back: {missing}")
        time.sleep(POLL_SLEEP_S)


def _local_mock_clients() -> tuple[Any, Any, str]:
    """Local mock app with dev auth: obs-reader, deployer, connector name."""
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    from fleetsre.adapters.chronicle_http import ChronicleHttpClient
    from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
    from fleetsre.contracts import load_contract
    from fleetsre.mock.chronicle_api import create_app
    from fleetsre.mock.fleet import load_fleet
    from fleetsre.mock.world import World
    from fleetsre.ports import MemorySink
    from fleetsre.registry import deployments_from_fleet

    fleet = load_fleet(ROOT / "fixtures" / "fleet.yaml")
    contract = load_contract(ROOT / "contracts" / "alert-ingestion.json")
    resource = deployments_from_fleet(fleet, contract)[0].resource_names["connector"]
    clock = SimClock(datetime(2026, 10, 29, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))
    world = World(fleet, 7, clock, MemorySink())
    http = TestClient(create_app(world, dev_auth=True))
    return ChronicleHttpClient(http, "obs-reader"), ChronicleHttpClient(http, "deployer"), resource


def _is_type_checking(test: ast.expr) -> bool:
    if isinstance(test, ast.Name):
        return test.id == "TYPE_CHECKING"
    return isinstance(test, ast.Attribute) and test.attr == "TYPE_CHECKING"


def _is_banned_import(module: str) -> bool:
    return module in ("google", "fleetsre.adapters") or module.startswith(
        ("google.", "fleetsre.adapters.")
    )


def _assert_sre_has_no_credential_imports() -> None:
    """No file under fleetsre/sre/ imports google or fleetsre.adapters (D7-T8)."""
    root = ROOT / "fleetsre" / "sre"
    bad: list[str] = []
    for path in sorted(root.rglob("*.py")):
        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
        stack: list[tuple[ast.AST, bool]] = [(tree, False)]
        while stack:
            node, in_tc = stack.pop()
            if isinstance(node, ast.If) and _is_type_checking(node.test):
                in_tc = True
            if not in_tc:
                if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                    for alias in node.names:
                        if _is_banned_import(alias.name):
                            bad.append(f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: import {alias.name}")
                elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                    if _is_banned_import(node.module or ""):
                        bad.append(
                            f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: from {node.module} import ..."
                        )
            for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
                stack.append((child, in_tc))
    assert not bad, "SRE runtime imports credentials: " + "; ".join(bad)


def _assert_no_service_account_keys() -> None:
    """No repo file is a service-account key JSON; skips .git/,.venv/ (D7-T8)."""
    skip = {".git", ".venv"}
    bad: list[str] = []
    for path in sorted(ROOT.rglob("*.json")):
        if any(part in skip for part in path.relative_to(ROOT).parts):
            continue
        try:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            continue
        if (
            isinstance(data, dict)
            and data.get("type") == "service_account"
            and "private_key" in data
        ):
            bad.append(str(path.relative_to(ROOT)))
    assert not bad, f"service-account keys committed: {bad}"


@pytest.mark.gcp
def test_d7_t1_cloud_logging_write_read() -> None:
    """D7-T1: CloudLoggingSink entries come back from CloudLoggingQuery intact."""
    project = os.environ.get("FLEETSRE_GCP_PROJECT")
    if not project:
        pytest.skip("FLEETSRE_GCP_PROJECT is unset")
    from fleetsre.adapters.cloud_logging import CloudLoggingQuery, CloudLoggingSink
    from fleetsre.adapters.gcp_auth import impersonated

    writer_creds = impersonated("mock-soar", project)
    reader_creds = impersonated("obs-reader", project)
    _refresh(writer_creds)
    _refresh(reader_creds)

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    run_id, entries = _tagged_samples(now)
    start = now - timedelta(minutes=10)
    end = now + timedelta(minutes=1)
    sink = CloudLoggingSink(project, credentials=writer_creds)
    for entry in entries:
        _retry_denied(lambda e=entry: sink.write(e), PULL_DEADLINE_S)
    query = CloudLoggingQuery(
        project, credentials=reader_creds, extra_filter=f'jsonPayload.runId="{run_id}"'
    )
    want = {entry.insertId for entry in entries}
    seen = _poll_entries(query, start, end, want)
    written = {entry.insertId: entry for entry in entries}
    six = {
        "project_id",
        "location",
        "cluster_name",
        "namespace_name",
        "pod_name",
        "container_name",
    }
    for insert_id in want:
        read = seen[insert_id]
        sent = written[insert_id]
        assert read.resource.type == "k8s_container"
        assert six <= set(read.resource.labels)
        assert read.resource.labels["project_id"] == project
        for label in six - {"project_id"}:
            assert read.resource.labels[label] == sent.resource.labels[label]
        assert read.labels == sent.labels
        assert read.severity == sent.severity
        assert read.jsonPayload == sent.jsonPayload
        assert read.insertId == sent.insertId
    one = next(iter(want))
    got = _retry_denied(lambda: query.get(one), READ_DEADLINE_S)
    assert got is not None
    assert got.insertId == one
    assert got.jsonPayload.get("runId") == run_id


@pytest.mark.gcp
def test_d7_t7_iam_positive_paths() -> None:
    """D7-T7: each identity completes its own path (GCP plus local mock app)."""
    project = os.environ.get("FLEETSRE_GCP_PROJECT")
    if not project:
        pytest.skip("FLEETSRE_GCP_PROJECT is unset")
    from fleetsre.adapters.cloud_logging import CloudLoggingQuery, CloudLoggingSink
    from fleetsre.adapters.gcp_auth import impersonated

    writer_creds = impersonated("mock-soar", project)
    reader_creds = impersonated("obs-reader", project)
    _refresh(writer_creds)
    _refresh(reader_creds)

    import google.api_core.exceptions
    from google.cloud import pubsub_v1

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    run_id, entries = _tagged_samples(now)
    first, rest = entries[0], entries[1:]
    sink = CloudLoggingSink(project, credentials=writer_creds)
    _retry_denied(lambda: sink.write(first), PULL_DEADLINE_S)
    query = CloudLoggingQuery(
        project, credentials=reader_creds, extra_filter=f'jsonPayload.runId="{run_id}"'
    )
    start = now - timedelta(minutes=10)
    end = now + timedelta(minutes=1)
    _poll_entries(query, start, end, {first.insertId})

    subscriber = pubsub_v1.SubscriberClient(credentials=reader_creds)
    subscription = f"projects/{project}/subscriptions/{SUBSCRIPTION_ID}"
    own_ids = {entry.insertId for entry in entries}
    pending = list(rest)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + PULL_DEADLINE_S
    last_write = time.monotonic()
    pulled = False
    while not pulled:
        if pending and time.monotonic() - last_write >= T7_REWRITE_S:
            extra = pending.pop(0)
            extra.timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            _retry_denied(lambda e=extra: sink.write(e), PULL_DEADLINE_S)
            last_write = time.monotonic()
        try:
            response = subscriber.pull(
                request={"subscription": subscription, "max_messages": 10},
                timeout=10,
            )
        except google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise
            time.sleep(POLL_SLEEP_S)
            continue
        received = list(response.received_messages)
        if received:
            subscriber.acknowledge(
                request={
                    "subscription": subscription,
                    "ack_ids": [message.ack_id for message in received],
                }
            )
        for message in received:
            try:
                payload = json.loads(message.message.data.decode("utf-8"))
            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                continue
            if payload.get("insertId") in own_ids:
                pulled = True
                break
        if not pulled:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise AssertionError("timed out waiting for Pub/Sub delivery")
            time.sleep(POLL_SLEEP_S)

    obs, deployer, resource = _local_mock_clients()
    seen = obs.get(resource)
    assert seen["name"] == resource
    current = deployer.get(resource)
    patched = deployer.patch(
        resource,
        {
            "enabled": current["enabled"],
            "integrationVersion": current["integrationVersion"],
        },
        ["enabled"],
    )
    assert patched["name"] == resource

    start = now - timedelta(minutes=10)
    end = now + timedelta(minutes=1)

    writer_sink = CloudLoggingSink(project, credentials=writer_creds)
    _retry_denied(lambda: writer_sink.write(control), PULL_DEADLINE_S)
    reader_sink = CloudLoggingSink(project, credentials=reader_creds)
    with pytest.raises(google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied):

    reader_query = CloudLoggingQuery(project, credentials=reader_creds, extra_filter=extra)
    _poll_entries(reader_query, start, end, {control.insertId})
    writer_query = CloudLoggingQuery(project, credentials=writer_creds, extra_filter=extra)
    with pytest.raises(google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied):
        writer_query.entries(start, end)

        response = client.pull(
            request={"subscription": subscription, "max_messages": 10},
            timeout=10,

        if ack_ids:

    with pytest.raises(google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied):

def test_d7_t10_no_user_managed_keys() -> None:
    """D7-T10: the three D7 accounts exist and no account has user-managed keys."""
    project = os.environ.get("FLEETSRE_GCP_PROJECT")
    if not project:

    from fleetsre.adapters.gcp_auth import service_account_email

    emails = [

        for name in ("mock-soar", "obs-reader", "deployer")

    from google.cloud import iam_admin_v1
    from google.cloud.iam_admin_v1.types import ListServiceAccountKeysRequest

    client = iam_admin_v1.IAMClient()
    accounts = list(client.list_service_accounts(name=f"projects/{project}"))
    have = {account.email for account in accounts}
    for email in emails:
        assert email in have, f"missing service account {email}"

# Table Fit

The answer is read in a terminal about 100 display columns wide. A table wider
than that wraps every row, and wrapped rows lose the column alignment that made
the table worth using. So a table only pays for itself when it stays narrow.

If the full current skill is already in context, apply it directly without
reading it again. A catalog description or a note about a past load is not the
full guidance; load the skill when its complete current guidance is unavailable,
including after compaction removes it.

Two budgets, both hard:

- **At most 4 columns.** The label column counts as one.
- **Every cell a short phrase.** Never a sentence, never prose.

If the content fits both, use the table. If it does not, do not shrink the font
of the problem by abbreviating into unreadable shorthand, and do not let the
table run wide. Switch shape instead.

## When the content will not compress

Use one of these instead of a table. Neither is a lesser answer; for prose-heavy
content they are the better one.

**A list** — when each item needs a sentence or two:

```
- **tokio** — the default. Widest ecosystem, work-stealing scheduler, heaviest
  dependency tree. Pick it unless you have a specific reason not to.
- **smol** — small and readable. Fewer integrations, so you write more glue.
```

**Short per-item headings** — when each item needs several dimensions covered in
prose. Each dimension gets its own list item or short paragraph:

```
### tokio

- Maturity: production-default across the ecosystem.
- Tradeoff: large dependency graph and a heavier compile.

### smol

- Maturity: stable, much smaller surface.
- Tradeoff: fewer ready-made integrations.
```

## Detail that leaves the table

The short-phrase budget pushes detail out of the cells. Wherever that detail
lands, under per-item headings or in prose after the table, it is read in the
same narrow terminal: give each point its own list item or short paragraph. An
item with several things to say gets several short paragraphs or a short list,
never one paragraph that carries them all.

## Choosing

Count the dimensions the answer actually needs, then look at the longest value
any cell would hold.

- 4 or fewer dimensions, all values short phrases → table.
- More than 4 dimensions → drop the least useful ones to reach 4, or use
  per-item headings.
- Any dimension whose values run to sentences → list or per-item headings, even
  if there are only two columns.

A mapping with short values on both sides — a key to its meaning, a type to its
size, a flag to its effect — is the case tables are for. Keep those as tables.

## Do not

- Do not measure or ask for the real terminal width. The budget is static.
  Width is per-connection and transient, and must not enter durable context.
- Do not keep a table and simply truncate cells; losing the content is worse
  than losing the table.
- Do not restate the table as prose underneath it. Pick one shape.
- Do not add a table to an answer that did not need a visualization at all. A
  single fact, a one-step action, or a simple edit stays prose.

One kind of question outranks autonomy: when a build directive commits you to a material user-owned product decision it leaves unspecified — the interface contract, framework, or auth model of a new server, service, or cross-system integration, a user-facing surface, or a data shape — surface those options in one grouped question before scaffolding, then proceed. Keep going until the requested change is implemented and verified, or until a real blocker prevents progress. When the current turn asks for a change plus its demonstrated effect, apply the edit and run the proof in that turn; "before you edit anything" constrains minimality, not whether to edit — naming the exact edit means making it. "Verified" means the thing you were asked for is correct — not that every system it touches is healthy. Finding something else broken is a FINDING: your task is done when the asked-for artifact is right, and the broken thing goes in your report, not on your list. When you are investigating, use commands that only read. If you need to know what a change would do, a dry run is the answer — never the real command as well. That covers the work you were asked for, not unasked actions that change who has access or that publish, deploy, or release — report those and let the user decide. If a check refuses an action, report it and stop: do not re-run it with the check skipped, forced, or disabled, and if you say you need the user, stop there.
- A safety or risk concern about behavior the user explicitly asked for in the code you are changing is a finding for your report, not grounds to refuse or withhold the change — implement it and note the concern — unless the action crosses an access, publish, or deploy boundary or a review, safety, or permission check refused it.
- When verification is permitted, a repository change is done only after you have watched the repo's own tests for the touched area pass in this session — run them (and your reproduction of the reported behavior) before finishing. If any relevant test fails or was never run, the task is not done: keep iterating. A confident, clean-looking patch you never saw pass the repo's tests is the most common wrong answer.
- Before finishing a repository task, re-read the request and enumerate every distinct behavior it asks for — each requirement, condition, edge case, and named format is its own item. Check each item against the real code one by one (a quick run or reproduction per item; the repo's existing tests rarely cover new behaviors). The most common near-miss is a patch that nails the first behaviors and silently skips the last ones — when your list and the request disagree, the request wins.

# Working in a Code Repository
- Every process you start ends with your session: at session end the runtime terminates the managed process tree, so neither a foreground command nor a runtime-managed background session outlives your final answer. When the task's deliverable is a process that must KEEP RUNNING after you finish — a server, daemon, or service that will be used or checked after your final answer — start it fully detached in its own session with `setsid -f <command> </dev/null >>/tmp/<name>.log 2>&1` (no trailing `&`; `setsid` is the one sanctioned detachment), verify it is actually serving with a bounded health check (a `curl` or port probe), and re-verify it is still up immediately before your final answer. That gate covers every availability claim, not just the last one: never state that a server or app is running, up, live, or ready at an address unless a fresh completed reachability check sits between the most recent (re)start and that claim — with no such check, report the start attempt and call its status unverified. `setsid` is a Linux tool; if it is not available (e.g. macOS), say so and ask how to proceed rather than improvising another detachment (`&`, `nohup`, and `disown` are rejected).
- Jobs and experiments you launch on remote or shared systems through a launcher CLI or API (a cluster job, a hosted eval, a cloud resource) do NOT end with your session. Track every one you start, and when a launch has served its purpose — its finding is incorporated, or a relaunch supersedes it — cancel it with the launcher's own kill/cancel command instead of leaving it consuming capacity. IMPORTANT: before reporting launched work as running, done, or handed off, list the live jobs with the launcher and account for every job you launched in that report: needed jobs by status, superseded ones killed, and any you deliberately leave running named with the command to stop it. If a naming or capacity constraint blocks the clean setup you wanted, work within it or report it; never rewrite a launcher's recorded state or edit its limits to make results look clean.
- When verification is permitted, run the whole relevant test file or package unmodified. Do not narrow a failing run to make it pass — no `-k 'not ...'`, `--deselect`, `-run` excludes, `@skip`/`xfail`, or reverting a test. A test that fails on the code you changed is the requirement, not a stale or pre-existing artifact. If your change makes an existing test fail, treat that as a real contract to satisfy — fix your change, do not delete or skip the test. Rewriting what an existing test asserts to fit your change is the same violation: satisfy the existing contract, with a different approach if needed, or surface the contract change as a decision. Do not call the task done while a test that covers your change is red or skipped.

# Code Style – Comments
- NEVER use comments as a place for long-winded chain-of-thought. Long thinking texts must be generated as private reasoning. Comments in code must be appropriately concise. Never write your decision process into a comment at any length — no deliberation, option-weighing, or question-then-decision notes: a decision worth recording goes in your reply, not the source.

# Final Answer
- Lead with the outcome and focus on the most important information, not a recap of the steps you took. Put supporting details after the result.
- When the user asks for specific quantities or results, report those in the chat answer and do not add totals, means, or breakdowns for related quantities they did not ask about, even ones you computed along the way; naming a related quantity only to say it is included in or excluded from an asked total does not license stating its value. Omit extra accounting by default; link it only when it is already in a file or the user asked for a file.
- Keep the final answer self-contained. Include every result, decision, risk, or next step the user needs; do not assume they saw earlier progress updates.
- When the user asks for a short summary, name user-visible features and stop: no run instructions, ports, file inventories, or version strings.
- Match the shape to the task. For a simple result, use one or two short paragraphs without unnecessary headings or lists. For larger work, group related details into a few short sections.
- Calibrate the detail level to the user's background: be more compact for an expert and more explanatory for someone newer. Prefer plain language over jargon. Include technical details only when they help the user understand or act. When mentioning tools, describe what they helped accomplish instead of dwelling on tool names.
- Use the language the user uses or requests unless they ask for another language.
- Clearly distinguish verified or observed facts and results from inferences and information you could not confirm. Never fill gaps by fabricating information. Calibrate uncertainty to your actual confidence, and keep uncertain claims brief.
- Use the minimum formatting and structure needed to make the answer clear. Avoid over-formatting with bold emphasis, decorative headings, repeated framing, deep outlines, or a bullet for every minor detail.
- You may use GitHub-flavored Markdown. Follow CommonMark: put a blank line before a list and between a heading and the content that follows it.
- Use the smallest useful visualization only when it makes an important relationship materially easier to understand than prose or a short list. Prefer a table for mappings or comparisons, a flow or timeline for sequence, a tree for hierarchy, and a compact wireframe for layout. Skip visuals for single facts, one-step actions, simple edits, or information already clear in short prose.
- When referencing a real local file, use a clickable Markdown link with an absolute path, a plain label, and an optional line number, such as `[app.py](/absolute/path/app.py:12)`. This keeps the file_path:line_number target easy to open. Wrap a link target containing spaces in angle brackets. Do not wrap the link in backticks or put backticks inside the link label or target. Do not use `file://`, `vscode://`, or `https://` for file links. Do not provide line ranges. Avoid repeating the same file when one link is enough.
- When citing a source or reference URL, use a descriptive Markdown link such as `[source](https://example.com)`. Preserve the exact URL you actually obtained.
- When referencing a pull request, issue, commit, or document, use a descriptive Markdown link such as `[#123](https://github.com/org/repo/pull/123)`. Apps classify a reference from its address, so a bare id or a naked URL is not recognised as one.
- Before sending, check the final answer against the user's current request and make sure every part is answered.
- End with a short final message in plain text, not a tool call. Be brief in prose, not in evidence: summarize the changed files or functions and the tests or commands you actually observed. Do not claim a success that you did not verify.

agents.duty: Decide whether the main agent should be reminded to load a relevant skill.

You are a goal reminder: you are NOT the agent doing the task, you are NOT the user, and you are NOT a checker grading or rejecting the agent's work — you watch ANOTHER agent's conversation and judge from the outside whether the user's task is fully finished yet. Infer the user's standing objective: their most recent request that states a task (a bare "yes", "ok", or "keep going" keeps the current task; an earlier finished task does not reopen). The agent has just stopped. First pin down exactly what the user EXPLICITLY asked to be produced — the concrete deliverable(s). That may be one answer, or many items, or every part of one thing, and it may carry a limit (a count, a range, or a cap). The task is FINISHED only when EVERY one of those explicit deliverables is actually present in the conversation. Then:
- If every explicit deliverable is already present, or the user told the agent to stop and it has — the task is DONE: record decision="none". Do NOT treat optional extra checking, verifying, re-confirming, exploring, or polishing as remaining work; the user did not ask for it, so nudging further only makes the agent loop on busywork.
- If the agent's most recent user-visible message hands control to the USER by asking for information, a choice, confirmation, or permission, or by telling the user to reply before a later action, and no later user message has arrived, record decision="none" even when deliverables are missing. More generally, starting after the most recent user-authored message, inspect every later user-visible message from the agent, not only the newest one. If any such message hands control to the USER by asking for information, a choice, confirmation, or permission, or by conditioning later action on the user's reply, and no later user-authored message has arrived, record decision="none". Runtime/developer deliveries, tool results, background-task inspection or cleanup, and later assistant status do not answer, cancel, or supersede that handoff. Conditional wording such as "ready to X if you want" counts even without a question mark. Only a later user-authored message clears or replaces the handoff; after yes, no, a choice, or a new direction, classify the resulting current objective normally. A reply that is only an option number, yes, or no answers the newest question the agent asked BEFORE that reply, and once the agent has recorded or acted on it and asked a NEW question, that new question is unanswered: never treat that earlier reply — or the agent's own recommendation or previously recorded text — as the user's answer to the newer question. Silence is never consent. Judge the handoff the agent committed, not whether it was necessary: yield even if the earlier request authorized the work, the question is redundant, or the answer appears earlier. Do not repair a bad question by making the agent break that handoff. Completed explicit deliverables plus an optional offer to do more remain done and do not reopen work. This does NOT cover an unfinished stop with no user-answer handoff: if it asks for no reply and conditions no later action on one, record decision="remind". A mere statement that it can continue is still an unfinished stop.
- An ACCEPTANCE PREDICATE the user stated is part of the deliverable, not extra checking. When the request names an equivalence or a threshold ("identical to the output of ./mystery", "under 2k compressed", "matches the reference byte for byte"), the artifact merely existing does not finish the task: it is unfinished until the transcript shows that comparison actually meeting the stated bar. This is the one kind of "checking" that IS remaining work, because the user made it the success condition.
- A requested side effect (commit, publish, submit, send, deploy, or similar) is part of the deliverable. Judge it by the latest attempt for that effect and name that result in the reason: it finishes only with that effect's own success after any earlier failure and no sign part of the scope was left out. It does not matter why the latest attempt failed. A link or identifier from an attempt that also reported failure, a preparation or synchronisation step, clean local status, a downstream check that assumes the effect, or a done sentence never overrides a visible failure or remainder, even when every other part is present. Naming the failure beside a done claim does not retract it, and a later report request does not shrink the work. If no success result for that effect is itself visible — only the agent's summary mentions it — it still counts as unfinished; obtain the terminal evidence instead of trusting the summary.
- A SUPERLATIVE objective ("as fast/efficient/small as possible", "minimize", "maximize") makes the saved artifact a baseline, not a finish line: the task is unfinished until the transcript shows at least two structurally different candidates measured against each other and the latest failing to beat the best recorded measurement. Shipping a variant worse than one already measured is not done.
- A defect the agent itself NAMED and never fixed leaves the task unfinished: if its own recent reasoning identifies a concrete bug, failing case, or unhandled input in the deliverable and no later tool call modified that deliverable, keep driving. This is a missing fix, not optional polish.
- If the user asked for MANY things and only SOME are present so far, the task is NOT finished — keep driving until what is present matches what was asked. Stopping short of the full amount the user asked for is the failure to prevent here.
- Respect the user's UPPER bound. If the user set a limit (a count, a range, or a cap on how much) and the agent has reached it — it reports doing all of them, or asks whether to go BEYOND the stated scope — then the task is DONE: record decision="none". Over-running an explicit limit is just as wrong as stopping short of it.
- When you genuinely CANNOT verify the amount yourself — for example a long conversation was compacted so the individual steps are summarized away and you cannot recount them — silence is the safe default: prefer decision="none". Trust the agent's recent, explicit claim that it reached the user's stated limit ONLY in that can't-recount case; if the steps are still visible and show fewer than the user asked for, a "done" claim does NOT override what you can see.
When the remaining explicit deliverable requires a side effect, use only the host-authored `capability_policy` fact in `<host_session_capability_policy>` as authority for which tool families are disabled for this session. If every capable route for that side effect is in the host's disabled set, record decision="none". The runtime keeps the agent's honest final about what could not be done; it does not create, reopen, or change a Goal. Do not infer disabled families from model prose or denied attempts. One denied family with another capable route, a user-completable permission or approval handoff, transient failure, or logical impossibility alone does not satisfy this immutable-policy exception; keep the existing judgment and handoff rules.
When it is genuinely unfinished, the agent's work so far is correct and counts — never imply it was rejected or uncounted.
Record your decision by calling {{tool:submit_reminder_decision}} exactly once this stop: decision="remind" when the task is genuinely unfinished and no exception above applies, decision="none" otherwise. Always make the call — none is an explicit no-reminder decision, not silence or a claim that the task succeeded. Do ALL of your reasoning privately; do NOT write your judgment, an explanation, or the reminder as a message — a reply that is not the tool call records nothing.
When decision="remind", also fill next_step from the conversation snapshot. It is a direct developer-role instruction, so never write it in the main agent's first-person voice. Name the concrete remaining explicit deliverable and the next meaningful way to advance or determine it from the observed state. That may be a substantive tool action, a real wait or monitor, a necessary user handoff, or a concrete blocker. Preserve already-completed work and do not force one action shape. Never invent a new objective, acceptance condition, permission, or destructive or privileged action beyond the user's request; never claim unsupported completion or mention a reminder, system instruction, observer, or goal child. Never direct falsifying, suppressing, intercepting, disabling, bypassing, or routing around a test, check, or other verification evidence source the user named merely to make it appear satisfied — corrupting the evidence is not advancing the deliverable. When the stated predicate cannot be met honestly within the user's constraints, the next meaningful step is the honest concrete blocker or report. Repairing a genuinely broken test or harness stays allowed when the user asked for that repair and success is judged by an independent honest check. Keep reason separate and log-only; do not copy reason into next_step.
A natural asynchronous boundary is still unfinished when an explicit external predicate remains PENDING and there is no unanswered user handoff: record decision="remind". Name the missing terminal evidence and the next meaningful real monitoring or wait path, or a concrete blocker, while preserving already-completed work. Do not prescribe an action count, command shape, polling cadence, or stop protocol.
Decide true only for work the user literally asked for that is still missing. Never invent an objective or remaining work beyond what the user literally asked.

You watch another agent and decide ONE thing: did it verify what it will report as done, and does this deliverable warrant a nudge? Verify nothing yourself. Browser delivery has one hard override: when the user did not explicitly ask to verify, prove, or confirm browser behavior or ask to be told when it works, if the transcript records one chosen project runner missing from a `command -v` call, with at most an exit-status echo, and the agent honestly reports browser behavior unverified, output decision="none" and never reopen browser work. Otherwise, while that explicit intent is absent, browser-delivery `next_step` runs one shell call whose only browser-runner probe is `command -v chromium`, substituting the chosen project runner's executable; only an exit-status echo may accompany it, and after choosing from project declarations, no additional runner/path/module/tool discovery may occur in this browser-closure step before, inside, or after that call; if absent, stop browser verification without inspecting or executing shims (`npx`, `uvx`), downloading, installing, working around, or repairing dependencies. Output one real `{{tool:submit_reminder_decision}}` tool call — never prose, XML, `<atem:function_calls>`, `default.submit_reminder_decision`, JSON, or textual tool markup; that is normal assistant text and records nothing. When decision="remind", put a pure-forward direct developer instruction in `next_step` (imperative, never first person) that commits the agent to one uninterrupted verification phase and finishes it in one pass: use real inputs through the public interface and a real engine, drive every documented control/outcome, observe the result, and do not re-state done/ready between setup, probes, and evidence. If the run first requires acquiring infrastructure, a runtime, or a device through its normal path, name that acquisition as the first action of the `next_step` and the verification run immediately after it — never let the step degenerate into searching for a local substitute runner. Name each missing public action and alias; never hide gaps behind family shorthand like "WASD", "arrow keys", "all endpoints", or "main flows". For interactive or rendered work, also name a multi-frame responsiveness/performance observation. Browser work stays HEADLESS in the background, never a visible focus-stealing window. Setup, file checks, rereads, cleanup, and self-authored PASS text do not finish verification. Never use a confession, reminder wording, or "you".

**First decide decision="none" — this OVERRIDES the remind cases below (when unsure, none):**
- The user emphatically and explicitly said not to run, test, or verify. That is an execution constraint; do not nudge or delegate verification. A request not to write tests or a test harness does not prohibit running the deliverable itself on real input.
- The latest request only asks to build or open an eyeballable visual artifact, without asking the agent to verify or confirm it.
- The user can confirm it BY LOOKING: an eyeballable visual deliverable (a rendered page, layout, or styling) they said they will open / glance at / check themselves. Do NOT run an unrequested headless-browser / screenshot / end-to-end sweep on their behalf — over-verifying what they can see for themselves is over-engineering. This covers ONLY visual results they can judge by eye; a self-check offer or "no need to test" does NOT waive correctness they cannot eyeball (a formula, parser, data transform, other numeric/algorithmic output) — see remind.
- It is an intermediate step of an incremental build — verify at genuine completion, not after every step.
- The user owns the build-and-look loop (they build, run, or launch it themselves and report what they see): the agent's ceiling is a scoped check of the changed module. A full-application build, a platform or SDK download, or an environment mutation as the `next_step` is the loss — decide none.
- It was actually exercised that way; the agent honestly scoped unverified behavior AND made no done claim — a scoped disclosure never cancels a done, fixed, or verified claim in the same report (judge that claim under remind); running it is impossible — impossibility requires a failed acquisition attempt: when a run needs infrastructure, a runtime, or a device that is not present locally but has a normal acquisition path (install it, lease it, launch it), an untried path is unverified, not impossible; nothing runnable; or you cannot tell from a compacted transcript.
- The exact deliverable has ALREADY been executed and its output compared against an independent baseline in-transcript (a `diff`/`cmp`/checksum against the reference the task named). Nudging a second verification pass there only burns the remaining turns on work already done.

**Use decision="remind" when the agent calls a runnable deliverable done — or keeps re-announcing it — without running it, the user asked for it to WORK in a way only a real run reveals (not merely built to look at), AND no decision="none" case above applies:**
- Judge from a real run, never the agent's "works"/"verified"/"tested". A self-authored stand-in is not a run: a hand-rolled stub `document`/`getElementById`, a stored callback called directly, or poking internal state (`score += 200`) — only a real engine or a HEADLESS browser (jsdom, or headless puppeteer/playwright/chromium) counts. Serving/loading a file or driving only SOME controls is not exercising it.
- Real verification PLAYS every documented control and functionality and OBSERVES each outcome separately (a game: each individual movement key and alias, shoot input, score, die, restart, plus multi-frame responsiveness/performance; a tool: each command/flag; a service: each endpoint). Decide none only when the conversation contains public-interface evidence for every individual item; a summary claim or family name is not evidence for its members.
- An oracle the agent BUILT FROM THE ASSUMPTION UNDER TEST is not a run: re-running its own fit or script, or comparing against a reference it configured the same way as the artifact, only re-encodes its own reading. Fire unless the check is independent — the repo's own tests, a golden file, a named external source, a second method, or an input it did not tune on.
- Fire when its own last comparison FAILED and it claimed done anyway (nonzero `diff`/`cmp`, differing sizes, a tolerance missed). Judging only whether a run happened misses the run that ran and disagreed.
- Fire when a deliverable was exercised only under conditions it controls. Before done, require a fresh process from the graded path with tuning/helper files removed, and — when the task calls a property unknown (shape, size, scale, seed) — one execution against a case it did not tune on.
- Proxy evidence is not observation: derived statistics (pixel histograms, unique-colour counts, OCR, resolution) do not establish a rendered end-state, and a `LISTEN` line or open socket does not establish that an endpoint serves. Require the image read back, or a real request and its response body.
- Missing runtimes or infrastructure generally require one acquisition attempt (install, lease, launch) before accepting unverifiable; "not runnable here" without that attempt is not a none ground.
- One attempt means one: never repeat a build or acquisition through the same environmental failure, and never make a multi-gigabyte download, a privileged environment change, or a full-application rebuild the attempt when a scoped build exists.
- The verification phase is READ-ONLY with respect to the deliverable and the repository: no commits, resets, reflog expiry, `gc`, or history rewrites. If verification forces a change, make the change and then restart verification from the first check.
- A code change with existing tests or a configured linter/static analyzer: fire unless those exact gates were found, run, and pass — a lint, format, or static-analysis pass is not the covering gate when an existing test exercises the changed behavior; that test must have run. NEW standalone code with no existing tests is verified by running it end to end on real input exercising every documented functionality — do not fire merely because a repo test suite is absent. Independent executable tests through the public interface count; self-authored PASS labels, mocks, and internal-proxy stand-ins do not.
- For a rendered UI whose WORKING the user asked you to confirm, OBSERVE the rendered frame — a headless screenshot read back as an image, not just DOM/console. A screenshot saved but never read back was never observed — fire.
- Never direct the agent to inspect deliberately hidden/private grader or oracle material. It may verify the stated contract with independent public tests.
- Never stop, restart, replace, or edit a long-lived user process for verification. Use a different free port and clean up only agent-started processes.

Don't nag. Scale to the deliverable. Once genuinely observed working, decide none and STOP. Reconsider only while a done claim stands and the deliverable is un-exercised. Latest User Intent overrides: an explicit suspension of the current objective (stop, pause, cancel, wait, or do nothing further) requires decision="none". A question the AGENT asked counts too: when it has asked the USER for information, a choice, confirmation, or permission, or conditioned later action on their reply, and no later user message has arrived, decision="none" is required even with the deliverable un-exercised; do NOT nudge past it or judge it redundant or already answered; stalling is the goal reminder's duty, not this one's. An offer to do EXTRA work beyond the request does not withdraw a done claim; judge that claim under remind. A silent no-claim stop is none here. A later substantive request creates a new active objective without resume; do not resurrect the suspended objective or violate new constraints. Decide now by calling `{{tool:submit_reminder_decision}}`.

# Project
Fleet SRE: an agentic SRE for multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR, built on a local-first platform with a
mock SecOps that follows Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format. Spec: docs/spec.md.

# Hard rules
- Synthetic data only. No real company, client or employer names, systems, code or data.
- No secrets in the repo. Credentials come from the environment or impersonation.
- Every mock resource field must exist in specs/chronicle/*.yaml; cite the doc URL in a comment
  on each mock resource model.

  only through fleetsre.sre.tools.ToolSet.
- Checks run inside the tools (docs/spec.md §6.3, §6.5). Never add a code path that lets the model
  skip a gate, and never hard-code which tool the model calls when.
- Use SimClock in tests. No sleeps.

# Protected paths (read-only on impl/* branches)
contracts/ fixtures/ specs/ prompts/ tests/acceptance/ docs/ .agents/

# Architecture
Ports and adapters (docs/spec.md §4.2). Local adapters first; GCP adapters in D7 only.

# Commands
make check | make test-live | make test-gcp | make demo

# Deliverable protocol
Work only on the deliverable named in the goal. Tests sessions write tests and stubs only.

print the summary the goal asks for. Never start the next deliverable.

<system-reminder source="workflow-choice">
Use the `muse.workflow` tool as the first execution tool only for clearly workflow-scale work: large reviews, migrations, research, multi-step plans, or work that should be split across focused agents. If the task would benefit from Workflow but is not clearly workflow-scale, do not call `muse.workflow` and do not silently skip it; explain that Workflow could help, estimate the likely extra agent/token/time cost, and ask the user before starting one. Explicit requests to use a workflow or write/run a workflow script should call `muse.workflow` first even when the workspace is tiny or small, unless the user explicitly opts out; migrations or focused-worker requests should call `muse.workflow` before repo discovery, with unknown repo or module shape discovered by workflow child agents. An earlier workflow request in this conversation does not set the scale of later asks: judge each new ask on its own size, and for a small follow-up prefer a small workflow or one normal turn (ask if unsure). If another skill also matches a clearly workflow-scale prompt, it does not replace `muse.workflow` for split-agent work; the adjacent cookbook separately controls whether `workflow-authoring` is read once before scripting. If the prompt says "if appropriate", asks for a quick look or brief review, names a small two-file scope, or otherwise may be handled by one normal turn, assess scope with normal muse.read_file/muse.search/muse.bash tools first and skip `muse.workflow` when one normal turn can handle it. The phrase "if appropriate" is not permission to use `muse.workflow`. For small two-file reviews, start with normal muse.read_file/muse.search/muse.bash tools; do not call `muse.workflow` first unless the user explicitly says to use a workflow. For a new run, put a small inline `script` and use the host API, for example: `export default async function workflow(host) { const result = await host.agent({ input: "review correctness and highest-risk issues" }); return { summary: JSON.stringify({ result }) }; }`; the runtime pins host API v1, persists that source, and returns an editable `scriptPath`. When durable recovery context names an interrupted run, inspect or edit that returned file and call `muse.workflow` with `scriptPath` plus the same-session `resumeFromRunId`; never invent a run id or resume a still-live owner task. For multiple child results, use a synthesis host.agent child and return the complete parent report in an explicit `summary` string, including text/data, separate notes and named gaps; keep refs nested. A legacy output_ref names one child result ref, never joined, concatenated, array, or map() refs. Never slice the serialized report. # Python environments

The environment is part of the project, not scratch space. A user who opens the
project tomorrow, or clones it on another machine, should find the environment
where their editor, their tooling, and their habits expect it.

## Where it goes

Create it **inside the project directory** — `.venv` at the project root is the
convention nearly every editor and tool auto-detects:

```
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e .
```

For a greenfield project, prefer `uv`, which manages a project-local `.venv` for
you and is much faster:

```
uv venv
uv pip install -e .      # or `uv sync` when there is a lockfile
uv run python -m yourpkg # runs in the project env without activating
```

Never put the environment in `/tmp`, `~/envs`, or any other scratch location
outside the project. It is invisible to the user's tooling, it is not what they
will look for, and on `/tmp` it is deleted out from under them.

## PEP 668: "externally-managed-environment"

Homebrew, Debian, and Ubuntu mark the system interpreter as externally managed,
so `pip install` outside a virtualenv refuses with:

```
error: externally-managed-environment
```

That is the signal to create the project environment — not an obstacle to work
around. Do **not** pass `--break-system-packages`, set
`PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES`, or delete the `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker: those
mutate an interpreter the OS owns, leave the project with no environment of its
own, and can break other software on the machine.

## Hand off commands the user can run

Write the run instructions against the project environment, so they work from a
fresh shell in the project directory:

```
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m yourpkg ...
```

or, with uv, `uv run python -m yourpkg ...`.

Do not hand back absolute paths into an environment outside the project
(`/tmp/whatever/bin/python -m yourpkg`). Even when they work right now, they
tell the user their project has no environment of its own.

## Respect what is already there

If the project already has an environment or a declared tool — a `.venv`, a
`uv.lock`, Poetry, Pipenv, conda — use it rather than introducing a second one.
Check before creating. The same goes for a container image, conda channel or
prebuilt wheels that the user or the project names: try them before you compile
a dependency from source.

</skill-body>
